pr_title: Fix Shelly sleepy RPC setup if device is already awake
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
When user setup a new sleepy device we don't know if the device is awake or already sleeping, so we used to wait for an event from the device, however if the user woke up the device (using the button) we can complete the device setup. Many users confuse when they see a new device added but without entities. The change here is trying to connect to the device silently on a background task so we don't care if the device is awake or not.

issue_context.title: Shelly Plus Smoke configured but without entities (reopened)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

This is basically a re-open of this issue, as the maintainer does not respond after multiple taggings: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/117818

The issue is, that Shelly Plus Smokes are added without any entities. That happens in 90% of the cases, sometimes they do get entities, after you retry **a lot** of times. I could not find a pattern what makes them appear after the Xth retry.

However, I have been able to kinda reproduce it while debug logging was enabled, please see the attached logfile.
What I've done during the timeframe the log shows:
* Added the Shelly Plus Smoke with IP 10.42.200.45 via discovery config flow
* After adding, the device had no entities, just the devive
* I tried hitting the "Reload" button on the device **multiple** times, no change. I did that because for another Shelly Smoke that eventually fixed that one.
* I waited until the device went back to sleep, then woke it up and immediately tried "Reload" and it had entities. *Maybe* the entities already appeared without me hitting reload and just waking up added them... I don't know

It's very easy to not get entities when adding a Shelly Plus Smoke, so it should be easy reproduceable.

I'm happy to help and try to reproduce and collect more info / logs!

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.8.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2024.8.1

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Shelly

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/shelly/

### Diagnostics information

[shelly-smoke.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16618457/shelly-smoke.log)


### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

```txt
Please see text in "The problem" above
```

Please see text in "The problem" above

Thanks @ezcGman, from you logs, while it is not the best user experience there is nothing different that what is currently happen with sleeping devices.

When you first wake the device HA detect the device, but we only collect the minimum data from the device to allow adding it.
When you add the device we just mark it as added (without entities) and wait for it to wake up again so we can collect all data from it. Although you are correct that the device is still awake, we don't really know it.
It can happen that hours pass from when the device was detected until you confirmed it in the UI.
On the 2nd wakeup device is already added so we collect all data to create entities.
From your log:
First step when you added the device:
```
2024-08-18 21:51:24.262 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.shelly] Setup for device smoke-alarm-level-1-corridor will resume when device is online
```
Second step when we detect the device is online and create the entities:
```
2024-08-18 21:53:30.160 DEBUG (MainThread) [custom_components.shelly] Device smoke-alarm-level-1-corridor is online, resuming setup
```

I will try to think of a logic to try to fetch data on the first step assuming the device may be online/offline and report back here, but anyhow this is not a specific bug for your case.

Hey @thecode 

sorry for the late reply! Totally forgot it...

> When you first wake the device HA detect the device, but we only collect the minimum data from the device to allow adding it.
> When you add the device we just mark it as added (without entities) and wait for it to wake up again so we can collect all data from it.

Why is it done this way though? Why is it required to wait until next wakeup? If you fetch the minimum data, why not directly fetch whatever you do when it wakes up again. You can still `try/except` it. If it works, it works, if not, it's tried after waking up again.

Thanks and greetings,

Andy!
#124547 should fix this after the next wake up.  Ideally we would create them a bit faster but that would be a much more invasive change

Repeating my question though: What is the challenge/issue to do this when adding the device directly? Is there some information missing that you only get after another wakeup? Or is it just the fear that device might have been gone to sleep again?

Anyways, that you need to wait for / need to force a wakeup to get entities for battery powered devices should be added to the docs page here: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/shelly/
This is definitely not obvious!

Ideally we create a repair issue telling the user they need to wake the device manually so we can connect and get the information needed to create the entities as otherwise all we have is some basic info from zeroconf about the device.

Once its setup for the first time the repair can be auto dismissed.

It may be a bit moot though since 2024.9.x will auto configure it as soon as it wakes up again and the problem will quickly fix itself in most cases which means the user would never see the repair issue anyways.

Thats quite a bit of work so it will need a champion who has some free cycles to work on that.

@bdraco The repair issue sounds like a middleground here, good idea!
However, I would kinda disagree on that "the user would never see the repair issue anyways", because as you said: They need to wake up the device. And you would only do this because the entities are missing. Why would you anyways wake it up again if it's added.
You only wake it up because it's missing all the entities or because there is the reqair issue. So it definitely would make sense.

I would again vote for **at least** adding that to the docs page; it's not obvious that you need to wake up the device again to get the entities added.

Thanks!

We can remove this condition on a cleanup PR which will remove handling for `None` as sleep period https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/9e762fa2223bd4c1610785108b7afa29f220b292/homeassistant/components/shelly/__init__.py#L280 since we already for it to `int`  - https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/9e762fa2223bd4c1610785108b7afa29f220b292/homeassistant/components/shelly/utils.py#L292-L294

This is a leftover from legacy code that did not store the sleep period but it is fixed for few years already.

This reverts https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/120582, it was used to add extra debug info since we investigated a race condition, but we should not log error here, with this PR it is important since we don't' want to log an error when we are not sure if the device is sleep or awake.
